pages.text: A lump of clay lay on the classroom table. Bobo shaped it into a bowl.
Bobo ran a finger along the side. This was where Bobo wanted a wave pattern.
Bobo set the bowl by the window. Bright sunlight fell on it.
Bobo stood right by the window. Those fingers itched to get started.
Bobo lifted the bowl onto a palm. "Still damp." It felt squishy.
Bobo drew a pattern with a twig. The side of the bowl pushed out of shape.
The bowl slumped to one side. Clay covered Bobo's hands.
Teacher Bau tapped a dry bowl. "Dry clay is hard like this."
A new bowl stood by the window. Bobo ran and played in the yard.
The bowl dried hard. Bobo drew long, wavy lines on it.
